theory.intro: To draw a **distance–time graph**, plot the point reached at the end of each stage and join consecutive points with straight lines. Time goes across, distance goes up. Read the vertical axis label: it may show distance from the start or total distance travelled.
facts: Time is always on the **horizontal** axis and distance on the **vertical** axis.
Plot the elapsed time (or clock time) and the distance reading at the end of each stage. Distance from the start decreases on a return journey; total distance travelled keeps increasing.
A stationary stage is drawn **horizontal** — time passes but the distance reading does not change.
On a graph of distance from the start, a return stage slopes down; the line touches the time axis when the traveller is back where they began.
Check the scale on both axes before plotting: one grid line rarely stands for one unit.
If a stage gives a speed and a time rather than a distance, work the distance out with $d=st$ first.
steps: Work out the time and distance reading at the end of each stage, using what the vertical axis measures.
Plot each of those points on the grid.
Join consecutive points with straight line segments.

workedExamples.question_text: A walker travels $9$ km from the start in $3$ hours at a steady speed. Draw the distance–time graph.
A cyclist rides $10$ km from the start in $40$ minutes, rests for $20$ minutes, then rides a further $14$ km in $40$ minutes. Each riding stage is at a steady speed. Draw the distance–time graph.

A runner travels $6$ km from home in $25$ minutes, rests for $10$ minutes, then returns home in $35$ minutes. Both running stages are at steady speeds. Draw a graph of distance from home against time.

The table gives a motorist's distance from the start. Draw the distance–time graph, taking the speed to be steady between consecutive readings.
$\begin{array}{c|rrrr}\text{Time (h)}&0&0.5&1.25&2.5\\\hline\text{Distance (km)}&0&18&18&42\end{array}$

A motorist leaves home at 11:10 am and travels $12$ km by 11:40 am. She stops for $20$ minutes, then travels a further $18$ km by 12:30 pm. She returns home in $60$ minutes. Each driving stage is at a steady speed. Draw the distance–time graph using minutes after 11:10 am.

Towns A and B are $24$ km apart along a road. Aria cycles from A to B at $12$ km/h. At the same time, Bo leaves B towards A at $8$ km/h, stops after $1$ hour for $30$ minutes, then continues at $8$ km/h to A. Draw both journeys on one graph, measuring distance from town A.
